cards.text: James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, is writing a letter, and he's just told his readers not to judge each other (James 1:1; 4:11-12). Now he says, "Come now," to people with BIG plans: today or tomorrow, they're off to some city for a year. Friend, I can see the color-coded calendar from here.

cards.question: These planners are heading off to some city for a year. What do they plan to do once they get there?

answers.text: Carry on business and make a profit
Build a house and settle down there
Visit family and rest for a while

cards.text: James doesn't even let them finish packing. He goes straight for one word in their plan: tomorrow.

cards.question: James tells these planners they know exactly what tomorrow will bring.

cards.text: And he's RIGHT: one day I'm on the counter for every birthday batch, the next I'm in the back of a junk drawer, and NOBODY sent me a calendar invite. Then James asks them, "What is your life?"

cards.question: James asks the planners, "What is your life?" What does he say they are?

cards.text: A mist, like the steam off a hot tray of cookies: you blink and it's GONE. So James tells the planners what they ought to say instead.

cards.question: James says they ought to say that if the Lord is ___, they will live and do this or that.

cards.text: But that's not how they're talking. James says, "As it is, you boast in your proud intentions."

cards.question: Then James adds that all such boasting is ___.

cards.text: James closes this part with one short line about knowing the right thing to do. Friend, this one finds me every time I walk past a dirty mixing bowl.

cards.question: Someone knows the right thing to do but doesn't do it. What does James say about that person?

cards.text: James says, "Come now," one more time. This time he's talking to the rich, and misery is coming their way.

cards.question: James tells the rich to ___ and wail over the misery to come upon them.

cards.text: Then James walks through their stuff like a home inspector who ONLY brings bad news. First up: their riches have rotted.

cards.question: The rich people's riches have rotted. What has happened to their clothes?
James says the rich people's gold and silver are still shining like new.

cards.text: And that corrosion doesn't just sit there quietly collecting dust. Trust me, friend, I spent YEARS sitting quietly collecting dust, so I'd know.

cards.question: James says the corrosion on the rich people's gold and silver will do what?

cards.text: James says it will consume their flesh like fire. Then he tells them, "You have hoarded treasure in the last days."
Now James points at the fields. Workers mowed those fields for the rich, and the rich held something back from them.

cards.question: What did the rich hold back from the workers who mowed their fields?

cards.text: Those withheld wages are crying out against the rich, and the harvesters are crying out too. I bet the rich figured nobody would ever hear a thing.

cards.question: James says the cries of the harvesters have reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts.

cards.text: Then James looks at how the rich have spent their days on earth.

cards.question: James says the rich have lived on earth in ___ and self-indulgence.

cards.text: He adds, "You have fattened your hearts in the day of slaughter." Then James says they have condemned and murdered the righteous, and whew, friend, he is NOT doing small talk today.

cards.question: James says the righteous, condemned and murdered by the rich, fought back against them.

findings.problem: The question uses "they" without identifying the planners, so it depends on the previous story card for its meaning. The question itself should name the planners.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "All such boasting" has no referent within the question and points back to the previous card's mention of the planners' proud intentions. The question should identify that boasting itself.
